audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls Ambessa's key ability "Repeating Dashes" in tldr, winCon, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.trading, dosFull[0].t, dosFull[0].d, phases[1].why, phases[3].why and phases[5].why.
audit.why: There is no ability called Repeating Dashes. Ambessa's abilities are Drakehound's Step (P), Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam (Q), Repudiation (W), Lacerate (E) and Public Execution (R). The passive is what produces the repeated dashing, so the intended referent is Drakehound's Step. The packet's suspectNames did not catch this because it only scans the content layer.
audit.corrected: Drakehound's Step — "entering an attack or movement command while casting an ability will cause Ambessa to dash a short distance once the ability is cast". Every cast is a potential dash, which is the real reason she weaves out of Tongue Lash.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json (ability list: Drakehound's Step, Cunning Sweep|Sundering Slam, Repudiation, Lacerate, Public Execution)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere warns against attacking Ambessa while Repudiation is bracing. wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1] instead describe vague "W empowerment".
audit.why: Repudiation "gains a shield, briefly braces herself, and then slams the ground... If she blocked any non-minion damage while bracing herself, this ability will deal increased damage." Tahm Kench stacks An Acquired Taste with basic attacks, so his natural instinct — keep autoing — is exactly what empowers the slam. This is the single most punishing habit in the matchup and the entry never mentions it.
audit.corrected: Hold autos through the brace and resume stacking after the slam. Damage you land during the brace is damage she gets back with interest.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json (W: "If she blocked any non-minion damage while bracing herself, this ability will deal increased damage", cd 18/17/16/15/14)

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] is the Level 6 stage and opens "Without your ultimate yet and still kiting-vulnerable".
audit.why: Devour is available at level 6. The stage text directly contradicts the stage it is attached to, and it is the stage where the reader most needs to know what their ultimate does and does not achieve.
audit.corrected: Devour is live at 6; what makes the stage hers is Public Execution answering it, not an absent ultimate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Public Execution is never named or described anywhere in the entry, despite being the ability that decides the level-6 stage the chart hands to Ambessa.
audit.why: It blinks her to the FARTHEST enemy champion in a line she chooses, suppresses on arrival, then stuns. Two things follow that matter: being the backmost champion in a line makes you the target rather than protecting you, and a suppress means you cannot act — so Thick Skin has to be converted before she commits, never during. It is also 130s at rank 1, the longest cooldown in either kit.
audit.corrected: Named, with the suppress consequence for Thick Skin timing and the 130s punish window.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json (R: "blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line of her choosing and suppresses them upon her arrival", cd 130/115/100, range 1250)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1], wants.you[0], late and whys[6] all describe "stun into Devour" or "Devour's empowered hold at 3 stacks"; late says "you stun and swallow".
audit.why: The Q stun at 3 stacks consumes all three stacks, and Devour requires 3 stacks. You cannot stun and swallow. There is also no such thing as an "empowered" Devour.
audit.corrected: Three stacks buys the stun or the eat. Against a dash chain the eat is correct, because a 1.5s stun does not stop Drakehound's Step from resetting the fight afterwards.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench)

audit.whatIsWrong: mid claims "At Level 6 Abyssal Voyage adds global threat and repositioning".
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is Tahm Kench's removed pre-rework ultimate. His W is Abyssal Dive, a short blink available from level 2. Nothing global arrives at 6 — Devour does.
audit.corrected: Replaced with what actually happens at 6 in this matchup: Public Execution.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench)

audit.why: I checked _missing-interactions.json, which lists "needs-antiheal: Ambessa sustains through chip damage (Public Execution (R))" for this matchup. That entry is a FALSE POSITIVE and I deliberately did not act on it. Riot's text for Public Execution contains no healing whatsoever; the "heal" flag in champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json is a bad derivation. Building Grievous Wounds against Ambessa on that basis would be a wasted item slot.
audit.corrected: No anti-heal advice added. The existing entry correctly does not mention it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json (R description contains no heal; flags list "heal" in error)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gives no numbers at all — "Her mobility. Q-stun around it."
audit.why: Repudiation is 18s at rank 1, Lacerate 13s, Cunning Sweep 14s, Public Execution 130s. The 130s ultimate is the window that actually decides whether you can walk at her.
audit.corrected: Real numbers inserted alongside the brace interaction.

notes:
NEW CLASS OF ERROR, not covered by the packet's suspectNames: the FULL layer for this matchup names Ambessa's key ability "Repeating Dashes", which is not an ability in the game at all. It appears in nine separate full-layer strings. suspectNames only scans champ-data/content/*.js, so full-layer ability names are currently unchecked across the entire site — worth a dedicated sweep. The intended referent is her passive, Drakehound's Step.

DATA-QUALITY WARNING — do not act on this one: _missing-interactions.json lists "needs-antiheal: Ambessa sustains through chip damage (Public Execution (R))" for tahmkench vs ambessa. Public Execution has no healing in Riot's text; champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json carries a spurious "heal" flag on R (and spurious "grounding" flags on both W and R, presumably derived from the words "slams the ground"). I did not write any anti-heal advice here. If other agents are consuming _missing-interactions.json uncritically, this matchup will get a wrong Grievous Wounds recommendation.

The highest-value addition I made is the Repudiation brace interaction: Tahm Kench stacks his passive with basic attacks, and basic attacks landed while she braces are exactly what empowers her slam. His core mechanic and her core mechanic are in direct conflict and the entry never said so.
